The text is parsed by a ready-made YAML 1.2 parser of a pinned version; on top of it stands the thin check\nof layer 1 ([layers of V7](../../common/LAYERS.md)): the rules `text` below, nothing beyond them.

Plain scalars are
recognized by the scalar table of [the section «Form»](#form-built-from-the-standard-files) by the style of the node —
a norm of this chapter, not the core schema of YAML 1.2 (core reads `0x10` and `0o7` as integers, and bool only as `true`,
`True`, `TRUE`).
The loader MUST accept exactly this text and MUST refuse everything beyond\nit (`refused:text`, N4).
- `bytes`: no BOM: U+FEFF as the first character of the file — refusal, further on — an ordinary character (`a﻿b` — a word).
- `bytes`: no C0 except TAB, LF and CR, no DEL and C1 (including U+0085 NEL), U+FFFE, U+FFFF, U+2028 and U+2029 — refusal.
- `bytes`: the same characters in a value after escaping (`\x07`, ` `, surrogates) — refusal.
- `bytes`: a lone CR — refusal, CRLF reads as LF.
- `tab`: `\t` and `\<TAB>` in double quotes — an escape, admissible.
- `document`: the root is a block mapping from column 1: a shifted document, a root in flow `{…}`, a list, a scalar, an\n  empty file — refusal.
- `refused`: an anchor `&`, an alias `*`, a tag `!…`, a merge key `<<`.
- `refused`: a mapping key and a list key.
- `refused`: a key said twice in one mapping (and in a flow `{a: 1, a: 2}`).
- `flow`: a lone `-` as a plain scalar in a flow (`[-, a]`, `[-]`, `a: [x, -]`, `{k: -}`) — refusal: in YAML 1.2.2 a plain\n  scalar in a flow does not start with `-` (yaml-test-suite G5U8, YJV2).

- `escape`: the result is a Unicode scalar value: a surrogate D800–DFFF (`\ud800`, `\U0000d800`, or the pair\n  `\ud83d\ude00` — YAML does not join surrogate pairs) — refusal; a Unicode scalar outside the BMP is admissible as a\n  literal `😀` or as `\U0001F600`.
- `comment`: `#` after a space — a comment, `#` inside a plain word (`a#b`, `counter# c`) — part of the word (YAML 1.2.2).
- `block`: leading empty lines of a block scalar are not deeper than its first non-empty line — otherwise refusal.
- `parser`: an empty element of a flow at the start or in the middle (`[a,,b]`, `[,a]`, `{a: 1,, b: 2}`) — a parse error.
- `parser`: a trailing comma at the end of a flow (`[a, b, ]`, `{k: v, }`) — admissible (YAML 1.2.2; yaml-test-suite\n  UDR7).
A lone `-` as a value in a block is the indicator of a list element, not a word (`unit: -` above a key of the same\nindentation — a parse error), in a flow `[-, a]` — refusal (`flow`).
An empty value (`key:` without a value) is neither a string nor a mapping: where the place needs a value, a form refusal\n(`refused:form`); an explicit «no» is written with the word `null` or `~`.

Float numbers in an accepted manifest are finite and in absolute value not greater than the limit of the scalar table\n(`float_max`) — after reading in binary64: a notation that rounds to this number (`1.7976931348623158e308`) is accepted.
A notation of a non-zero number that reads as zero (underflow, `1e-400`) is `refused:form`.
